sentences.text:
Brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present appeal are that appellant/claimant (hereinafter referred .
to as the 'claimant') filed a claim petition, seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in an accident which occurred on 29.01.2008.
According to the claimant, on the fateful day, he was travelling in his car bearing registration No. HP-38-2500.
When he reached near Village Bhadal, Tehsil Nurpur, District Kangra, a Tractor bearing Registration No. HP- 38-9790, which had only one head light, hit the car.
The claimant sustained injuries and fell unconscious.
He was taken to the hospital at Pathankot.
As per the the claimant, as the accident was a result of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor, he was entitled for compensation to the tune of Rs. 2 lac.
The claim petition was resisted by the respondents before the learned Tribunal.

Besides other objections that were taken with regard to the claim of the claimant,
one of the objection taken was that the accident in fact was a result of the rash and negligent driving on part of the claimant himself, which was evident from the contents of the FIR which was registered after the incident occured.

3. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, learned Tribunal framed the following issues:-
.
"1.
Whether injured Rajinder singh suffered injuries due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle (Tractor) bearing registration No. HP-38-9790, as alleged?
OPP 2.
If issue No.1 is proved in affirmative, to what amount of compensation, the petitioner is entitled and from whom?
OPP r Whether petition is not maintainable, as alleged?
OPR 4.
Whether petitioner has no cause of action and locus- standi to file present petition, as alleged?
OPR 5. Whether petition is bad for mis-joinder and non- joinder of necessary parties, as alleged?

sentences.text:
The Award was passed by the learned Tribunal on 28.06.2013 and as the judgment which has been appended .
with the application was passed by the learned Trial Court on 21.10.2014 i.e., after the passing of the Award by the learned Tribunal, therefore, the application is allowed and the judgment appended therewith is taken on record, as it will facilitate the adjudication of the appeal.
6. I have learned Counsel for the appellant and also learned Senior Counsel appearing for respondent No.1 and have also gone through the Award passed by the learned Tribunal and the record of the case.
7.

A perusal of the Award passed by the learned Tribunal demonstrates that after taking into consideration the statements of the witnesses, who deposed before the said Tribunal, learned Tribunal returned the findings that the claimant had miserably failed to demonstrate that the accident in question took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor bearing Registration No. HP-38- 9790.

During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the appellant from the evidence on record could not demonstrate that the findings so recorded by the learned Tribunal were perverse findings or a result of misreading or mis-appreciation .
of the statements of the witnesses on record.

Incidentally, there is also on record Ex.PW1/A, copy of FIR No. 32 of 2008, dated 29.01.2008, registered under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of Indian Penal Code, which was registered at the behest of complainant Rakesh Kumar.

In terms of contents thereof, the accident had taken place on account of the rash and negilgent driving of the appellant,
who was driving the Maruti Car bearing registration No. HP-38-2500.
There is also on record the complaint that was filed by the appellant to the Superintendent of Police Ex.PW2/A.

It was mentioned in this complaint that taking advantage of the fact that the appellant had fallen unconscious immediately after the accident, which took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor, the vehicles were removed from the spot and false case was registered against the appellant.
8. From the statement of PW2 Head Constable Joginder Singh, this complaint stands proved and his statement also reveals that the inquiry of the complaint was assigned to him.

Copy of the inquiry report Ex.RW/A is to the effect that there was no merit in the complaint so filed by the appellant.
.

Not only this, now it is otherwise evident from the judgment that has been passed by the learned Trial Court, copy whereof is appended with the application, filed under Order 41, Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, that it was the appellant who has been convicted for rash and negligent driving in the trial that took place pursuant to the lodging of the FIR.

Therefore, as this Court does Rajinder Singh vs Shri Rakesh Kumar And Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169634043/
4 not finds any illegality or perversity in the Award passed by the learned Tribunal and further as this Court does not finds any merit in the appeal, the same is dismissed.
